topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text: I opened the box, my hands steady, the air thick with the unspoken. Here lay items not for me, yet they told a story I could read. Old newspapers, a half-used journal with penciled thoughts, a hand-knitted scarf worn thin by time. I could have handed it off, a simple gesture. Instead, I delved deeper, curious and then committed. I pieced together a brief life, a fragment of someone’s past. My room, now my domain, held echoes of another. I arranged the contents with care on the table, a silent tribute to the unseen. The package was a bridge, not a barrier, and I stood on the threshold of connection, wanting to honor it.
